docs.title: Fork ID 9 to 12
docs.text:
💡 For CDK fork ID9 chains NOT attached to Agglayer (Isolated), they can ignore section 4.

💡 For CDK fork ID9 chains attached to Agglayer, follow steps in sections 1 to 5. This is a coordinated effort between Polygon and the Implementation Provider.

docs.title: 1. Summary of the Procedure
docs.text:
To initiate a CDK chain upgrade, the Implementation Provider can request support from Polygon by submitting the “Request Help for an Issue with an Existing CDK Chain” through the service desk.

CDK Service Desk Example Request

Polygon will then collaborate with the Implementation Provider to schedule the UTC timing and dates for the upgrade.

This planning enables the Implementation Provider to schedule testnet and mainnet maintenance windows for the respective networks, ensuring proper communication and coordination with their communities.

See Example Maintenance Communication to Network Partners Implementation Providers can prepare for the customer network chains.

The high-level steps in the collaborative process are:

  1. Implementation Provider halting the sequencer,
  2. Implementation Provider can send & execute the upgrade transaction,
  3. Implementation Provider upgrades components to Fork 12 stack,
  4. Implementation Provider restarts the components.
  5. Polygon updates the Permissionless node attached to the Agglayer for that chain.

docs.title: 2. CDK Components Versions
docs.text:
Please read carefully to fully understand the new architecture before starting the process: https://docs.polygon.technology/cdk/getting-started/cdk-erigon/

The table below lists the CDK Fork ID 9 components and the new CDK FEP Fork ID 12 components.

💡 Please note: Latest CDK FEP Fork ID 12 components are listed in the Polygon Knowledge Layer

CDK Components Fork ID 9 CDK Components Fork ID 12 CDK Validium nodeSequence senderAggregator 0.6.7+cdk.1 CDK Erigon RPC & CDK node cdk-erigon:v2.1.x CDK nodeSequence senderAggregator cdk:v0.3.x Tx pool manager zkevm-pool-manager Tx pool manager zkevm-pool-manager use latest tag Prover v6.0.0 Prover zkevm-prover v8.0.0-RC14 CDK data availability v0.0.7 CDK data availability cdk-data-availability use latest tag zkEVM rollup node v6.0.0 zkEVM rollup node N/A Contracts v6.0.0 Contracts zkevm-contracts Bridge service v0.4.2-cdk.1 Bridge service zkevm-bridge-service Bridge UI Polygon Portal Bridge UI Polygon Portal

docs.title: 3. Implementation Provider Preparation Steps
docs.text:
The Implementation Provider must prepare in advance for the upgrade to ensure a smooth transition from fork ID 9 to fork ID 12. Failure to complete these steps ahead of time could result in delays or even cancellation of the scheduled upgrade.

  1. The Implementation Provider downloads CDK Fork 12 components in advance so they are ready to deploy.
  2. Map to the latest prover files which can be found here: https://storage.googleapis.com/zkevm/zkproverc/v8.0.0-rc.9-fork.12.tgz
  3. Scale up the number of provers in advance. It is recommended that you at least double the number of provers up and running for the scheduled upgrade maintenance window.
    • Ensure all (majority) of the network batches are verified before starting the upgrade process, otherwise there will be additional downtime as we wait for the network to be ready.
  4. Setting up your CDK Erigon node.
    • Please see the cdk-erigon readme for information on prereqs, configuration files and running cdk-erigon.
  5. Required CDK-Node pre syncing.
  6. Run CDK-Node aggregator component in sync only mode in advance to populate its database.
  7. Run CDK-Node l1infotreesync component in advance to populate the sequence sender database.
  8. Required Erigon pre-syncing:
    • Generate data stream files from the current cdk-validium-node database.
      • Tool and instructions can be found here:
        • https://github.com/0xPolygonHermez/zkevm-node/tree/develop/tools/datastreamer
    • Use the Erigon tool (from cdk-erigon repo) to serve the DS:
      • go run ./zk/debug_tools/datastream-host --file /path/to/directory
      • Start CDK-Erigon, which reads from this datastream (provide zkevm.l2-datastreamer-url: 127.0.0.1:6900 in the config).
    • Wait for it to sync to the tip.
    • CDK-Erigon can be stopped. The generated files will be used later during the upgrade process.

The whole process should look more or less like this: 

# PREREQUISITES: Install GO 1.23
WORK_DIR=/tmp

cd $WORK_DIR
git clone https://github.com/0xPolygonHermez/zkevm-node.git
cd $WORK_DIR/zkevm-node/tools/datastreamer
vim config/tool.config.toml
# Edit [StateDB] section with your StateDB credentials
make generate-file

cd $WORK_DIR
git clone https://github.com/0xPolygonHermez/cdk-erigon.git
cd $WORK_DIR/cdk-erigon
go run ./zk/debug_tools/datastream-host \
    --file $WORK_DIR/zkevm-node/tools/datastreamer/datastream

# Bring up Erigon pointing to that DS (localhost:6900 if running locally)
# and let it fully sync to the end of the DS.

docs.title: 4. Polygon Preparation Steps
docs.text:
1. Polygon will collaborate with the Implementation Provider to agree on the scheduled and dates for the upgrade which will incorporate any required time locks.
  2. For chains attached to the Polygon Agglayer, Polygon will handle steps to upgrade the permissionless node.
  3. See example communication that Implementation Providers can use to prepare their customer network partners and communities.

docs.title: 5. Operational Steps
docs.text:
Please Note: To avoid creating reorgs or other unwanted situations, it’s important that all L2 transactions are verified before performing a fork upgrade. This means all batches should be closed, sequenced, and verified on L1.

Please Note: IP Partner Rollup admin can send & execute the fork ID upgrade transaction.

  1. Stop the sequencer.

  2. Reconfigure the node to enforce sequencer stops at a specific batch_num:

    • Get the current batch number from StateDB:
    -- Note resulting value as X:
SELECT batch_num, wip FROM state.batch WHERE wip IS true;
    • Edit node configuration:
    # SEQUENCER CONFIG
# Where X is the batch number obtained from the SQL query:
Sequencer.Finalizer.HaltOnBatchNumber = X+1
# Optional: Reduce batch time to avoid excessive downtime
Sequencer.Finalizer.BatchMaxDeltaTimestamp = "120s" # 1800s

    # SEQUENCE SENDER CONFIG
# Optional: Reduce sending time to avoid excessive downtime
SequenceSender.WaitPeriodSendSequence = "10s" # 60s
SequenceSender.LastBatchVirtualizationTimeMaxWaitPeriod = "30s" # 600s

    # AGGREGATOR CONFIG
# Recommended: Reduce verify interval to avoid excessive downtime
Aggregator.VerifyProofInterval = "5m"
    • Restart the sequencer, sequence sender, and aggregator to apply these configs.
    • Check that the sequencer halts when reaching batch X+1.
    • Wait until all pending batches are virtualized and verified (X):
    -- Both queries should return X
SELECT max(batch_num) FROM state.virtual_batch;
SELECT max(batch_num) FROM state.verified_batch;

  3. Stop all services (node, prover/executor, bridge).

  4. Implementation Provider Rollup admin: Upgrade Smart Contract.

    • Upgrade rollup to fork 12.
    • Wait for the Tx to be finalized.

docs.title: Steps to Deploy CDK FEP Fork 12 Components
docs.text:
1. It is recommended to back up your DAC node by taking a snapshot of the DAC database.

    • Locate Your PostgreSQL Instance:
      • Identify the PostgreSQL host, port, database name (dac_db), and the username (master_user) configured for your DAC node. These values can typically be found in your environment’s configuration or .env files.
      • Run the pg_dump Command:
      • Use the pg_dump command to create a backup of your DAC database. Replace the placeholders with your specific values:
      • pg_dump -U master_user -d dac_db -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432 > dac.db.sql
      • Verify the Backup:
      • After running the command, ensure that the dac.db.sql file has been created and contains the database snapshot.

  2. With the network stopped, repeat Erigon sync to get it fully synced to the current state.

    • This instance is ready to act as Sequencer and/or RPC. Clone the whole Erigon config/datadir as many times as instances are needed. Pick one to be the new Sequencer (by setting the environment variable CDK_ERIGON_SEQUENCER=1), and configure all other instances (permissionless RPCs) to point to the Sequencer:
    zkevm.l2-sequencer-rpc-url: "http://sequencer-fqdn-or-ip:8123"
zkevm.l2-datastreamer-url: "sequencer-fqdn-or-ip:6900"

  3. Start the stateless Executor.

  4. Start CDK-Erigon Sequencer
    • On a fork upgrade, once the upgrade Tx is finalized you can start the sequencer. Once started, check logs and ensure new blocks are generated with new forkid.
      • You would expect to see starting block #5796790 as forkid 12. If you see the starting block 5796790 as fork id 9 there is a problem. If the new block is on the old fork id 9, you need to resync sequencer from scratch or get one of the rpc datadirs (that were synced till the halt and are currenctly stopped) and replace it to become the new sequencer.
  5. Verify in the sequencer’s logs that new blocks are being generated with fork ID 12.
  6. Start the Pool Manager (if used/needed).
  7. Start CDK-Erigon RPCs (if used/needed).
  8. Start the Bridge.
  9. Start the CDK aggregator and Sequence Sender components.
  10. Start the stateless Prover.

docs.title: Polygon Steps for CDK Chains Attached to the Agglayer
docs.text: Polygon’s DevOps team will be accountable for upgrading the Agglayer permissionless nodes during the upgrade process.

docs.title: Post-Upgrade Validations
docs.text:
1. Implementation Provider will test the batch lifecycle.
  2. Implementation Provider will test the bridge.

docs.title: Devnet Deployment Guide
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive, step-by-step guide to deploying a Pessimistic Proof (PP) (cdk-opgeth-sovereign) production-like devnet.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, ensure you have:

  • A valid L1 RPC URL
  • A wallet address with Sepolia testnet funds (deployer)
  • Docker (or any other container orchestrator of your choice)
  • Cast
  • Polycli
  • Reference Repo (configuration files used in the guide)

Export these variables:

export L1_RPC_URL=https://...
export SEPOLIA_PROVIDER=${L1_RPC_URL}
export DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

💡 The values shown are specific to this example — be sure to replace them with those relevant to your own setup.

docs.title: Step 1: Submit a Request
docs.text:
To initiate the rollup creation:

  1. The Implementation Provider (IP) must submit a request to Polygon Labs.
  2. Use the Polygon Support Portal to raise a support ticket.

docs.title: Required Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description Example Rollup Type Type of rollup Pessimistic Proofs (PP) Chain ID Unique identifier for your rollup 473 Admin Address Your control address for rollup modifications 0xBe46896822BD1d415522F3a5629Fe28447b95563 Sequencer Address Used by AggKit, must be under your control 0x0769fcb9ca9369b0494567038E5d1f27f0CBE0aC Gas Token Address Token or zero address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 Sequencer URL (Not used for PP) https://... Datastream URL (Not used for OP) https://... Network Name Final network name (non-editable) bali-36-op

docs.title: Step 2: Setup by Polygon Labs
docs.text:
Once approved:

  • Polygon Labs provisions your Rollup.
  • A transaction is recorded (e.g., example).

You will receive:

  • combined.json: Core deployment details
  • genesis-base.json: Needed for genesis generation

💡 Secure these files. They are required for further deployment steps.

docs.title: Option Selection
docs.text:
Choose one:

  • Option 1 (Recommended): Merge OP + Polygon Genesis with pre-deployed contracts.
  • Option 2: Manual L2 contract deployment.

This guide focuses on Option 1.

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Environment Setup

Checkout the Desired Version. We will be usingv10.0.0-rc.7 in this example 

git clone https://github.com/0xPolygonHermez/zkevm-contracts.git
cd zkevm-contracts
git checkout v10.0.0-rc.7

Install dependencies as described in the repo’s README.

docs.title: L2 Deployment (Using op-deployer)
docs.text:
To set up your Layer 2 (L2) network using the OP Stack, we recommend starting with the official Optimism L2 Rollup tutorial. This guide provides a practical reference based on that tutorial and leverages the op-deployer tool to streamline the deployment process.

💡 All commands in this section are executed from the root directory of your project.

  1. Initialize deployer Folder
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/deployer:/deployer -it us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-deployer:v0.0.13 \
    init \
    --l1-chain-id 11155111 \
    --l2-chain-ids "${CHAIN_ID}" \
    --workdir /deployer

  1. Edit intent.toml with your parameters.

  2. Deploy L1 Contracts

docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/deployer:/deployer -it us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-deployer:v0.0.13 \
    apply \
    --workdir /deployer \
    --l1-rpc-url ${L1_RPC_URL} \
    --private-key ${DEPLOYER_PRIVATE_KEY}
  1. Merge Genesis Files

Next, you’ll need to combine the polygon-genesis.json file with the OP Stack’s genesis.json. The recommended approach is to embed the contents of polygon-genesis.json directly into the op-deployer state. 

# extract the allocs
cat deployer/state.json | jq -r '.opChainDeployments[].allocs' | base64 -d | gzip -d > allocs.json

# merge
jq -s add allocs.json files/polygon-genesis.json | gzip | base64 > merge

# create a copy of the original state
cp deployer/state.json deployer/original-state.json

# replace the original allocs by the merged
cat deployer/state.json | jq ".opChainDeployments[].allocs=\"$( cat merge )\"" > state.json && mv state.json deployer/state.json

# cleanup
rm allocs.json merge

  1. Generate Files
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/deployer:/deployer -it us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-deployer:v0.0.13 \
   inspect genesis \
   --workdir /deployer "${CHAIN_ID}" > ./deployer/genesis.json

docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/deployer:/deployer -it us-docker.pkg.dev/oplabs-tools-artifacts/images/op-deployer:v0.0.13 \
   inspect rollup \
   --workdir /deployer "${CHAIN_ID}" > ./deployer/rollup.json

docs.title: L2 to L1
docs.text:
1. Initiate a Deposit

Start by making a deposit from L2 using the following command: 

polycli ulxly bridge asset \
    --bridge-address ${BRIDGE_ADDRESS} \
    --destination-network 0 \
    --private-key ${TEST_PRIVATE_KEY} \
    --rpc-url http://$(docker compose port op-geth 8545) \
    --value $(date +%s) \
    --destination-address ${TEST_ADDRESS}

  1. Wait for the Pessimistic Proof

Once the deposit is made, a pessimistic proof will be generated. After this proof is available, the deposit becomes eligible for claiming.

  1. Verify the Deposit Status

You can check the status of your deposit by querying the bridge service: 

curl -s http://$(docker compose port bridge 8080)/bridges/${TEST_ADDRESS} | jq '.'
{
  "deposits": [
    {
      "leaf_type": 0,
      "orig_net": 0,
      "orig_addr": "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
      "amount": "1746047601",
      "dest_net": 0,
      "dest_addr": "0xda9f3DCA867C4Bc7b1f8e2DB47Aa8C338Ba2e056",
      "block_num": "14136",
      "deposit_cnt": 0,
      "network_id": 36,
      "tx_hash": "0x4a5d4914e4ae315af941e1fad2b2aac54dfd6c9bc2ca6033e0ea0b325fbcd90e",
      "claim_tx_hash": "",
      "metadata": "0x",
      "ready_for_claim": true,
      "global_index": "150323855360"
    }
  ],
  "total_cnt": "1"
}

✅ If “ready_for_claim”: true, the deposit is ready to be claimed.

  1. Claim the Deposit on L1

Run the following command to claim the deposit: 

polycli ulxly claim asset \
    --bridge-address ${BRIDGE_ADDRESS} \
    --bridge-service-url http://$(docker compose port bridge 8080) \
    --deposit-count 0 \
    --destination-address ${TEST_ADDRESS} \
    --deposit-network ${ROLLUP_ID} \
    --private-key ${TEST_PRIVATE_KEY} \
    --rpc-url ${L1_RPC_URL}

  1. Confirm the Claim

Finally, confirm that the deposit has been successfully claimed by checking the balance of the destination address: 

cast balance ${TEST_ADDRESS} --ether --rpc-url=${L1_RPC_URL}

Use the command below to run the Kurtosis package:

kurtosis run \

polycli ulxly bridge asset \
  --bridge-address $(kurtosis service exec cdk contracts-001 'jq -r '.polygonZkEVMBridgeAddress' /opt/zkevm/combined.json') \

docs.title: Why choose CDK?
docs.text: This page covers the key features and capabilities of the Agglayer Chain Development Kit (CDK), including supported execution stacks, EVM compatibility, Agglayer integration, performance benchmarks, rollup modes, and target audiences. Whether you’re a developer, startup founder, or enterprise team, this guide will help you understand how CDK can power your custom Ethereum Layer 2 chain.

docs.title: Multistack Support
docs.text: CDK gives developers the flexibility to choose from multiple execution stacks based on their technical goals. Use cdk-opgeth for OP Stack familiarity and Geth-based performance, or choose cdk-erigon for deep customization and advanced ZK integration. More stacks will be supported in the future.

docs.title: EVM Compatibility
docs.text: CDK chains are fully EVM-equivalent. Developers can deploy existing smart contracts, use familiar Ethereum tooling, and preserve current workflows without rewrites or reconfiguration.

docs.title: Native Agglayer Integration
docs.text: All CDK chains connect to Agglayer by default. This provides unified liquidity, shared state, and seamless messaging across chains—without requiring additional setup or bridging infrastructure.

docs.title: High Performance
docs.text:
• cdk-opgeth supports 60 to 100+ million gas per second (Mgas/s) when paired with the G2 sequencer.
  • cdk-erigon delivers up to 60+ Mgas/s in burst throughput, with native support for ZK proving and advanced configuration.

docs.title: Flexible Rollup Modes
docs.text: Soon, both cdk-opgeth and cdk-erigon will support zkRollup, Validium, and Sovereign modes. Developers can choose the configuration that best balances cost, trust assumptions, and data availability for their specific use case.

docs.title: Web3 Developers
docs.text: Deploy purpose-built Layer 2 chains with precise control over execution logic, rollup mode, data availability, and token design. CDK supports EVM tooling and workflows out of the box.

docs.title: Founders and Builders

Launch performant, production-ready chains quickly with help from trusted implementation providers:

docs.title: Enterprises
docs.text:
Build secure and scalable blockchain infrastructure with enterprise-level configurability. For example, cdk-erigon offers full customization, including:

  • Three live ZK-secured rollup modes

docs.title: What is CDK?
docs.text:
The Agglayer Chain Development Kit (CDK) is a multistack toolkit for building custom Ethereum Layer 2 (L2) chains. Each CDK chain is natively connected to Agglayer, enabling seamless cross-chain interoperability, shared liquidity, and unified state across an expanding ecosystem of L2s.

CDK supports multiple execution stacks so developers can choose the architecture that best suits their project. Current options include:

  • cdk-opgeth: A high-performance, OP Stack-style client built on Ethereum’s most widely adopted execution client, Geth.
  • cdk-erigon: A customizable, ZK-secure client with advanced configuration options and full Agglayer connectivity.

More stacks will be added soon. Whether you’re building a DeFi protocol, launching a high-throughput chain, or creating a security-first enterprise appchain, CDK provides the flexibility to launch on your terms—while benefiting from unified liquidity across the Agglayer network.

pragma solidity ^0.8.0;

contract YieldFarmIntegration {
    struct Farm {
        IVaultBridgeToken stakingToken;
        IERC20 rewardToken;
        uint256 rewardRate;
        uint256 lastUpdateTime;
        uint256 rewardPerTokenStored;
    }

    struct UserRewards {
        uint256 userRewardPerTokenPaid;
        uint256 rewards;
    }

    mapping(uint256 => Farm) public farms;
    mapping(uint256 => mapping(address => uint256)) public balances;
    mapping(uint256 => mapping(address => UserRewards)) public userRewards;

    function stake(uint256 farmId, uint256 amount) external {
        Farm storage farm = farms[farmId];

        updateReward(farmId, msg.sender);

        balances[farmId][msg.sender] += amount;
        farm.stakingToken.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);

        emit Staked(msg.sender, farmId, amount);
    }

    function claimRewards(uint256 farmId) external {
        updateReward(farmId, msg.sender);

        uint256 reward = userRewards[farmId][msg.sender].rewards;
        if (reward > 0) {
            userRewards[farmId][msg.sender].rewards = 0;
            farms[farmId].rewardToken.transfer(msg.sender, reward);
            emit RewardClaimed(msg.sender, farmId, reward);
        }
    }

    function updateReward(uint256 farmId, address account) internal {
        Farm storage farm = farms[farmId];
        farm.rewardPerTokenStored = rewardPerToken(farmId);
        farm.lastUpdateTime = block.timestamp;

        if (account != address(0)) {
            userRewards[farmId][account].rewards = earned(farmId, account);
            userRewards[farmId][account].userRewardPerTokenPaid = farm.rewardPerTokenStored;
        }
    }

    function rewardPerToken(uint256 farmId) public view returns (uint256) {
        Farm storage farm = farms[farmId];
        uint256 totalStaked = farm.stakingToken.balanceOf(address(this));

        if (totalStaked == 0) {
            return farm.rewardPerTokenStored;
        }

        return farm.rewardPerTokenStored + 
            (((block.timestamp - farm.lastUpdateTime) * farm.rewardRate * 1e18) / totalStaked);
    }

    function earned(uint256 farmId, address account) public view returns (uint256) {
        return (balances[farmId][account] * 
            (rewardPerToken(farmId) - userRewards[farmId][account].userRewardPerTokenPaid)) / 1e18 +
            userRewards[farmId][account].rewards;
    }

    event Staked(address indexed user, uint256 indexed farmId, uint256 amount);
    event RewardClaimed(address indexed user, uint256 indexed farmId, uint256 amount);
}

docs.title: Vault Bridge Token
docs.text:
The primary contract implementing ERC-20, ERC-4626, and Unified Bridge extension interfaces.

Key Features: - Asset deposits and vbToken minting (1:1 ratio) - Integration with external yield vaults - Cross-chain bridging capabilities - Migration support for Layer 2 assets

Interfaces: - IERC20: Standard token functionality - IERC4626: Vault deposit/withdraw operations - IUnifiedBridgeExtension: Cross-chain bridge integration

Use Cases: - Direct asset deposits for yield generation - Cross-chain vbToken transfers - Integration with existing ERC-4626 compatible protocols

docs.title: Migration Manager
docs.text:
Coordinates asset migration from Layer Y Native Converters to Layer X Vault Bridge Tokens.

Key Features: - Cross-chain asset migration coordination - Batch processing for gas efficiency - Security validation and anti-fraud measures - Shared infrastructure across all vbTokens

Responsibilities: - Process migration requests from Native Converters - Validate cross-chain messages and proofs - Execute deposits into Vault Bridge Tokens - Maintain migration audit trails

docs.title: 1. Basic Integration
docs.text:
The simplest way to integrate with Vault Bridge is using the standard ERC-4626 interface:

// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity ^0.8.0;

import "@openzeppelin/contracts/interfaces/IERC4626.sol";
import "@openzeppelin/contracts/interfaces/IERC20.sol";

contract SimpleVaultBridgeIntegration {
    IERC4626 public immutable vaultBridgeToken;
    IERC20 public immutable underlyingAsset;

    constructor(address _vaultBridgeToken, address _underlyingAsset) {
        vaultBridgeToken = IERC4626(_vaultBridgeToken);
        underlyingAsset = IERC20(_underlyingAsset);
    }

    function depositToVault(uint256 amount) external {
        // Transfer underlying asset from user
        underlyingAsset.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);

        // Approve Vault Bridge Token to spend the asset
        underlyingAsset.approve(address(vaultBridgeToken), amount);

        // Deposit and receive vbTokens
        uint256 shares = vaultBridgeToken.deposit(amount, msg.sender);

        emit Deposited(msg.sender, amount, shares);
    }

    function withdrawFromVault(uint256 shares) external {
        // Redeem vbTokens for underlying assets
        uint256 assets = vaultBridgeToken.redeem(shares, msg.sender, msg.sender);

        emit Withdrawn(msg.sender, shares, assets);
    }

    event Deposited(address indexed user, uint256 assets, uint256 shares);
    event Withdrawn(address indexed user, uint256 shares, uint256 assets);
}

contract WETHVaultIntegration {

    IWETH public immutable WETH;

    constructor(address _vbWETH, address _WETH) {
        vbWETH = IERC4626(_vbWETH);
        WETH = IWETH(_WETH);

        // Convert ETH to WETH
        WETH.deposit{value: msg.value}();

        // Approve and deposit WETH to vault
        WETH.approve(address(vbWETH), msg.value);
        uint256 shares = vbWETH.deposit(msg.value, msg.sender);

        emit ETHDeposited(msg.sender, msg.value, shares);
    }

        // Redeem vbWETH for WETH

        // Convert WETH back to ETH and send to user
        WETH.withdraw(wethAmount);
        payable(msg.sender).transfer(wethAmount);

        emit ETHWithdrawn(msg.sender, shares, wethAmount);
    }

    receive() external payable {}

    event ETHDeposited(address indexed user, uint256 ethAmount, uint256 shares);
    event ETHWithdrawn(address indexed user, uint256 shares, uint256 ethAmount);
}

contract Layer2VaultIntegration {
    INativeConverter public immutable nativeConverter;
    IERC20 public immutable underlyingAsset;
    IERC20 public immutable vbToken;

    constructor(
        address _nativeConverter,
        address _underlyingAsset,
        address _vbToken
    ) {
        nativeConverter = INativeConverter(_nativeConverter);
        underlyingAsset = IERC20(_underlyingAsset);
        vbToken = IERC20(_vbToken);
    }

    function convertToVbToken(uint256 amount) external {
        // Transfer underlying asset from user
        underlyingAsset.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);

        // Approve Native Converter
        underlyingAsset.approve(address(nativeConverter), amount);

        // Convert to vbTokens
        uint256 vbTokens = nativeConverter.convert(amount, msg.sender);

        emit Converted(msg.sender, amount, vbTokens);

    function deconvertFromVbToken(uint256 vbTokenAmount) external {
        // Transfer vbTokens from user
        vbToken.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), vbTokenAmount);

        // Deconvert to underlying assets
        uint256 assets = nativeConverter.deconvert(vbTokenAmount, msg.sender);

        emit Deconverted(msg.sender, vbTokenAmount, assets);
    }

    event Converted(address indexed user, uint256 assets, uint256 vbTokens);
    event Deconverted(address indexed user, uint256 vbTokens, uint256 assets);
}

            return tx.hash;

            throw error;
        }

            return tx.hash;
        } catch (error) {
            console.error('Withdrawal failed:', error);
            throw error;
        }
    }

        return await this.vaultBridgeToken.balanceOf(userAddress);
    }

    async getAssetValue(shares) {
        return await this.vaultBridgeToken.convertToAssets(shares);
    }

pragma solidity ^0.8.0;

import "@openzeppelin/contracts/interfaces/IERC4626.sol";
import "@openzeppelin/contracts/interfaces/IERC20.sol";

contract VaultBridgeLendingPool {
    struct Market {
        IERC4626 vbToken;          // Vault Bridge Token
        IERC20 underlyingAsset;    // Original asset (WETH, USDC, etc.)
        uint256 totalDeposits;     // Total vbTokens deposited
        uint256 totalBorrows;      // Total underlying assets borrowed
        uint256 interestRate;      // Current interest rate
        uint256 lastUpdateTime;    // Last interest calculation
    }

    mapping(address => Market) public markets;
    mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public userDeposits;
    mapping(address => mapping(address => uint256)) public userBorrows;

    event MarketAdded(address indexed vbToken, address indexed underlying);
    event Deposited(address indexed user, address indexed market, uint256 amount);
    event Borrowed(address indexed user, address indexed market, uint256 amount);

    function addMarket(
        address vbTokenAddress,
        address underlyingAsset,
        uint256 initialRate
    ) external onlyOwner {
        markets[vbTokenAddress] = Market({
            vbToken: IERC4626(vbTokenAddress),
            underlyingAsset: IERC20(underlyingAsset),
            totalDeposits: 0,
            totalBorrows: 0,
            interestRate: initialRate,
            lastUpdateTime: block.timestamp
        });

        emit MarketAdded(vbTokenAddress, underlyingAsset);
    }

    function supply(address vbTokenAddress, uint256 amount) external {
        Market storage market = markets[vbTokenAddress];
        require(address(market.vbToken) != address(0), "Market not found");

        // Transfer vbTokens from user
        market.vbToken.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);

        // Update user deposits
        userDeposits[msg.sender][vbTokenAddress] += amount;
        market.totalDeposits += amount;

        emit Deposited(msg.sender, vbTokenAddress, amount);
    }

    function borrow(address vbTokenAddress, uint256 amount) external {
        Market storage market = markets[vbTokenAddress];
        require(address(market.vbToken) != address(0), "Market not found");

        // Check user has sufficient collateral
        require(_hasCollateral(msg.sender, vbTokenAddress, amount), "Insufficient collateral");

        // Convert vbTokens to underlying assets for borrowing
        uint256 underlyingAmount = market.vbToken.redeem(amount, address(this), address(this));

        // Transfer underlying assets to user
        market.underlyingAsset.transfer(msg.sender, underlyingAmount);

        // Update user borrows
        userBorrows[msg.sender][vbTokenAddress] += underlyingAmount;
        market.totalBorrows += underlyingAmount;

        emit Borrowed(msg.sender, vbTokenAddress, underlyingAmount);
    }

    function _hasCollateral(address user, address market, uint256 amount) internal view returns (bool) {
        // Implement collateral calculation logic
        // This is simplified - real implementation would check across all markets
        uint256 userCollateral = userDeposits[user][market];
        return userCollateral >= amount * 150 / 100; // 150% collateralization ratio
    }
}

contract VaultBridgeAMM {
    struct Pool {
        IERC4626 vbTokenA;
        IERC4626 vbTokenB;
        uint256 reserveA;
        uint256 reserveB;
        uint256 totalLiquidity;
        mapping(address => uint256) liquidityBalance;
    }

    mapping(bytes32 => Pool) public pools;

    function createPool(
        address vbTokenA,
        address vbTokenB,
        uint256 amountA,
        uint256 amountB
    ) external returns (bytes32 poolId) {
        poolId = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(vbTokenA, vbTokenB));

        Pool storage pool = pools[poolId];
        pool.vbTokenA = IERC4626(vbTokenA);
        pool.vbTokenB = IERC4626(vbTokenB);

        // Transfer initial liquidity
        pool.vbTokenA.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amountA);
        pool.vbTokenB.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amountB);

        pool.reserveA = amountA;
        pool.reserveB = amountB;
        pool.totalLiquidity = sqrt(amountA * amountB);
        pool.liquidityBalance[msg.sender] = pool.totalLiquidity;

        emit PoolCreated(poolId, vbTokenA, vbTokenB, amountA, amountB);
    }

    function swap(
        bytes32 poolId,
        address tokenIn,
        uint256 amountIn,
        uint256 minAmountOut
    ) external returns (uint256 amountOut) {
        Pool storage pool = pools[poolId];
        require(pool.totalLiquidity > 0, "Pool does not exist");

        bool isTokenA = address(pool.vbTokenA) == tokenIn;
        require(isTokenA || address(pool.vbTokenB) == tokenIn, "Invalid token");

        if (isTokenA) {
            amountOut = getAmountOut(amountIn, pool.reserveA, pool.reserveB);
            require(amountOut >= minAmountOut, "Insufficient output amount");

            pool.vbTokenA.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amountIn);
            pool.vbTokenB.transfer(msg.sender, amountOut);

            pool.reserveA += amountIn;
            pool.reserveB -= amountOut;
        } else {
            amountOut = getAmountOut(amountIn, pool.reserveB, pool.reserveA);
            require(amountOut >= minAmountOut, "Insufficient output amount");

            pool.vbTokenB.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amountIn);
            pool.vbTokenA.transfer(msg.sender, amountOut);

            pool.reserveB += amountIn;
            pool.reserveA -= amountOut;
        }

        emit Swap(poolId, msg.sender, tokenIn, amountIn, amountOut);
    }

    function getAmountOut(uint256 amountIn, uint256 reserveIn, uint256 reserveOut) 
        public 
        pure 
        returns (uint256) 
    {
        require(amountIn > 0 && reserveIn > 0 && reserveOut > 0, "Invalid amounts");
        uint256 amountInWithFee = amountIn * 997; // 0.3% fee
        uint256 numerator = amountInWithFee * reserveOut;
        uint256 denominator = reserveIn * 1000 + amountInWithFee;
        return numerator / denominator;
    }

    function sqrt(uint256 x) internal pure returns (uint256) {
        if (x == 0) return 0;
        uint256 z = (x + 1) / 2;
        uint256 y = x;
        while (z < y) {
            y = z;
            z = (x / z + z) / 2;
        }
        return y;
    }

    event PoolCreated(bytes32 indexed poolId, address tokenA, address tokenB, uint256 amountA, uint256 amountB);
    event Swap(bytes32 indexed poolId, address indexed user, address tokenIn, uint256 amountIn, uint256 amountOut);
}

contract VaultBridgeYieldFarm {
    struct Farm {
        IERC4626 stakingToken;     // vbToken to stake
        IERC20 rewardToken;        // Reward token
        uint256 rewardPerBlock;    // Rewards distributed per block
        uint256 lastRewardBlock;   // Last block rewards were calculated
        uint256 accRewardPerShare; // Accumulated rewards per share
        uint256 totalStaked;       // Total vbTokens staked
    }

    struct UserInfo {
        uint256 amount;        // vbTokens staked by user
        uint256 rewardDebt;    // Reward debt for reward calculation
        uint256 pendingReward; // Pending rewards to be claimed
    }

    mapping(uint256 => Farm) public farms;
    mapping(uint256 => mapping(address => UserInfo)) public userInfo;
    uint256 public farmCount;

    event FarmCreated(uint256 indexed farmId, address stakingToken, address rewardToken);
    event Staked(address indexed user, uint256 indexed farmId, uint256 amount);
    event Withdrawn(address indexed user, uint256 indexed farmId, uint256 amount);
    event RewardClaimed(address indexed user, uint256 indexed farmId, uint256 amount);

    function createFarm(
        address stakingToken,
        address rewardToken,
        uint256 rewardPerBlock
    ) external onlyOwner returns (uint256 farmId) {
        farmId = farmCount++;

        farms[farmId] = Farm({
            stakingToken: IERC4626(stakingToken),
            rewardToken: IERC20(rewardToken),
            rewardPerBlock: rewardPerBlock,
            lastRewardBlock: block.number,
            accRewardPerShare: 0,
            totalStaked: 0
        });

        emit FarmCreated(farmId, stakingToken, rewardToken);
    }

    function stake(uint256 farmId, uint256 amount) external {
        Farm storage farm = farms[farmId];
        UserInfo storage user = userInfo[farmId][msg.sender];

        updateFarm(farmId);

        if (user.amount > 0) {
            uint256 pending = user.amount * farm.accRewardPerShare / 1e12 - user.rewardDebt;
            user.pendingReward += pending;
        }

        if (amount > 0) {
            farm.stakingToken.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);
            user.amount += amount;
            farm.totalStaked += amount;
        }

        user.rewardDebt = user.amount * farm.accRewardPerShare / 1e12;

        emit Staked(msg.sender, farmId, amount);
    }

    function withdraw(uint256 farmId, uint256 amount) external {
        Farm storage farm = farms[farmId];
        UserInfo storage user = userInfo[farmId][msg.sender];
        require(user.amount >= amount, "Insufficient staked amount");

        updateFarm(farmId);

        uint256 pending = user.amount * farm.accRewardPerShare / 1e12 - user.rewardDebt;
        user.pendingReward += pending;

        if (amount > 0) {
            user.amount -= amount;
            farm.totalStaked -= amount;
            farm.stakingToken.transfer(msg.sender, amount);
        }

        user.rewardDebt = user.amount * farm.accRewardPerShare / 1e12;

        emit Withdrawn(msg.sender, farmId, amount);
    }

    function claimReward(uint256 farmId) external {
        Farm storage farm = farms[farmId];
        UserInfo storage user = userInfo[farmId][msg.sender];

        updateFarm(farmId);

        uint256 pending = user.amount * farm.accRewardPerShare / 1e12 - user.rewardDebt;
        uint256 totalReward = user.pendingReward + pending;

        if (totalReward > 0) {
            user.pendingReward = 0;
            farm.rewardToken.transfer(msg.sender, totalReward);
            emit RewardClaimed(msg.sender, farmId, totalReward);
        }

        user.rewardDebt = user.amount * farm.accRewardPerShare / 1e12;
    }

    function updateFarm(uint256 farmId) public {
        Farm storage farm = farms[farmId];

        if (block.number <= farm.lastRewardBlock) return;

        if (farm.totalStaked == 0) {
            farm.lastRewardBlock = block.number;
            return;
        }

        uint256 blocks = block.number - farm.lastRewardBlock;
        uint256 reward = blocks * farm.rewardPerBlock;

        farm.accRewardPerShare += reward * 1e12 / farm.totalStaked;
        farm.lastRewardBlock = block.number;
    }
}

contract CrossChainYieldAggregator {
    struct Strategy {
        uint32 chainId;
        address vbToken;
        address yieldProtocol;
        uint256 currentYield;
        uint256 tvl;
        bool active;
    }

    mapping(uint256 => Strategy) public strategies;
    mapping(address => mapping(uint256 => uint256)) public userAllocations;
    uint256 public strategyCount;

    // Cross-chain messaging interface
    interface ICrossChainMessenger {
        function sendMessage(uint32 destinationChain, bytes calldata message) external;
    }

    ICrossChainMessenger public messenger;

    event StrategyAdded(uint256 indexed strategyId, uint32 chainId, address vbToken);
    event FundsAllocated(address indexed user, uint256 indexed strategyId, uint256 amount);
    event YieldHarvested(uint256 indexed strategyId, uint256 amount);

    function addStrategy(
        uint32 chainId,
        address vbToken,
        address yieldProtocol
    ) external onlyOwner returns (uint256 strategyId) {
        strategyId = strategyCount++;

        strategies[strategyId] = Strategy({
            chainId: chainId,
            vbToken: vbToken,
            yieldProtocol: yieldProtocol,
            currentYield: 0,
            tvl: 0,
            active: true
        });

        emit StrategyAdded(strategyId, chainId, vbToken);
    }

    function allocateToStrategy(uint256 strategyId, uint256 amount) external {
        Strategy storage strategy = strategies[strategyId];
        require(strategy.active, "Strategy not active");

        if (strategy.chainId == block.chainid) {
            // Local allocation
            _allocateLocal(strategyId, amount);
        } else {
            // Cross-chain allocation
            _allocateCrossChain(strategyId, amount);
        }

        userAllocations[msg.sender][strategyId] += amount;
        strategy.tvl += amount;

        emit FundsAllocated(msg.sender, strategyId, amount);
    }

    function _allocateLocal(uint256 strategyId, uint256 amount) internal {
        Strategy storage strategy = strategies[strategyId];

        // Transfer vbTokens to strategy contract
        IERC20(strategy.vbToken).transferFrom(msg.sender, strategy.yieldProtocol, amount);
    }

    function _allocateCrossChain(uint256 strategyId, uint256 amount) internal {
        Strategy storage strategy = strategies[strategyId];

        // Bridge vbTokens to target chain
        bytes memory message = abi.encode(
            "allocate",
            strategyId,
            msg.sender,
            amount
        );

        messenger.sendMessage(strategy.chainId, message);
    }

    function getBestStrategy() external view returns (uint256 bestStrategyId) {
        uint256 bestYield = 0;

        for (uint256 i = 0; i < strategyCount; i++) {
            if (strategies[i].active && strategies[i].currentYield > bestYield) {
                bestYield = strategies[i].currentYield;
                bestStrategyId = i;
            }
        }
    }
}

contract ChainRevenueDistributor {
    struct RevenueStream {
        address source;        // Vault Bridge Token address
        uint256 totalRevenue;  // Total revenue accumulated
        uint256 distributed;   // Already distributed amount
        mapping(address => uint256) allocations; // Recipient allocations
        address[] recipients;  // List of recipients
    }

    mapping(address => RevenueStream) public revenueStreams;
    mapping(address => bool) public authorizedSources;

    address public chainTreasury;
    address public operationsFund;
    address public developmentFund;

    // Default allocation percentages (basis points, 10000 = 100%)
    uint256 public treasuryAllocation = 4000;  // 40%
    uint256 public operationsAllocation = 3000; // 30%
    uint256 public developmentAllocation = 3000; // 30%

    event RevenueReceived(address indexed source, uint256 amount);
    event RevenueDistributed(address indexed recipient, uint256 amount);
    event AllocationUpdated(address indexed recipient, uint256 newAllocation);

    constructor(
        address _chainTreasury,
        address _operationsFund,
        address _developmentFund
    ) {
        chainTreasury = _chainTreasury;
        operationsFund = _operationsFund;
        developmentFund = _developmentFund;
    }

    function authorizeRevenueSource(address source) external onlyOwner {
        authorizedSources[source] = true;
    }

    function receiveRevenue(address source) external payable {
        require(authorizedSources[source], "Unauthorized source");
        require(msg.value > 0, "No revenue to distribute");

        RevenueStream storage stream = revenueStreams[source];
        stream.totalRevenue += msg.value;

        emit RevenueReceived(source, msg.value);

        // Auto-distribute if configured
        _distributeRevenue(source);
    }

    function _distributeRevenue(address source) internal {
        RevenueStream storage stream = revenueStreams[source];
        uint256 pendingRevenue = stream.totalRevenue - stream.distributed;

        if (pendingRevenue == 0) return;

        // Calculate distributions
        uint256 treasuryAmount = pendingRevenue * treasuryAllocation / 10000;
        uint256 operationsAmount = pendingRevenue * operationsAllocation / 10000;
        uint256 developmentAmount = pendingRevenue * developmentAllocation / 10000;

        // Distribute to recipients
        if (treasuryAmount > 0) {
            payable(chainTreasury).transfer(treasuryAmount);
            emit RevenueDistributed(chainTreasury, treasuryAmount);
        }

        if (operationsAmount > 0) {
            payable(operationsFund).transfer(operationsAmount);
            emit RevenueDistributed(operationsFund, operationsAmount);
        }

        if (developmentAmount > 0) {
            payable(developmentFund).transfer(developmentAmount);
            emit RevenueDistributed(developmentFund, developmentAmount);
        }

        stream.distributed += (treasuryAmount + operationsAmount + developmentAmount);
    }

    function updateAllocations(
        uint256 _treasuryAllocation,
        uint256 _operationsAllocation,
        uint256 _developmentAllocation
    ) external onlyOwner {
        require(
            _treasuryAllocation + _operationsAllocation + _developmentAllocation == 10000,
            "Allocations must sum to 100%"
        );

        treasuryAllocation = _treasuryAllocation;
        operationsAllocation = _operationsAllocation;
        developmentAllocation = _developmentAllocation;
    }

    function manualDistribute(address source) external {
        _distributeRevenue(source);
    }
}

contract VaultBridgeGasSponsorship {
    using ECDSA for bytes32;

    struct SponsorshipPool {
        uint256 balance;
        uint256 dailyLimit;
        uint256 dailySpent;
        uint256 lastResetDay;
        mapping(address => bool) authorizedSpenders;
        mapping(address => uint256) userDailySpent;
    }

    mapping(address => SponsorshipPool) public sponsorshipPools;
    mapping(bytes32 => bool) public usedNonces;

    address public revenueDistributor;
    uint256 public gasPrice;

    event SponsorshipPoolFunded(address indexed pool, uint256 amount);
    event TransactionSponsored(address indexed user, address indexed pool, uint256 gasUsed);
    event DailyLimitUpdated(address indexed pool, uint256 newLimit);

    modifier onlyAuthorizedSpender(address pool) {
        require(sponsorshipPools[pool].authorizedSpenders[msg.sender], "Not authorized spender");
        _;
    }

    function fundSponsorshipPool(address poolAddress) external payable {
        require(msg.value > 0, "Must send ETH to fund pool");

        sponsorshipPools[poolAddress].balance += msg.value;
        emit SponsorshipPoolFunded(poolAddress, msg.value);
    }

    function sponsorTransaction(
        address user,
        address poolAddress,
        uint256 gasUsed,
        bytes32 nonce,
        bytes calldata signature
    ) external onlyAuthorizedSpender(poolAddress) {
        require(!usedNonces[nonce], "Nonce already used");

        // Verify signature
        bytes32 messageHash = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(user, poolAddress, gasUsed, nonce));
        address signer = messageHash.toEthSignedMessageHash().recover(signature);
        require(signer == user, "Invalid signature");

        SponsorshipPool storage pool = sponsorshipPools[poolAddress];

        // Reset daily limits if needed
        uint256 currentDay = block.timestamp / 86400;
        if (currentDay > pool.lastResetDay) {
            pool.dailySpent = 0;
            pool.lastResetDay = currentDay;
        }

        uint256 gasCost = gasUsed * gasPrice;

        require(pool.balance >= gasCost, "Insufficient pool balance");
        require(pool.dailySpent + gasCost <= pool.dailyLimit, "Daily limit exceeded");
        require(pool.userDailySpent[user] + gasCost <= pool.dailyLimit / 10, "User daily limit exceeded");

        // Update balances and limits
        pool.balance -= gasCost;
        pool.dailySpent += gasCost;
        pool.userDailySpent[user] += gasCost;
        usedNonces[nonce] = true;

        // Refund gas to user
        payable(user).transfer(gasCost);

        emit TransactionSponsored(user, poolAddress, gasUsed);
    }

    function setDailyLimit(address poolAddress, uint256 newLimit) external onlyOwner {
        sponsorshipPools[poolAddress].dailyLimit = newLimit;
        emit DailyLimitUpdated(poolAddress, newLimit);
    }

    function authorizeSpender(address poolAddress, address spender) external onlyOwner {
        sponsorshipPools[poolAddress].authorizedSpenders[spender] = true;
    }

    // Function to receive revenue from Vault Bridge
    receive() external payable {
        require(msg.sender == revenueDistributor, "Only revenue distributor");
        // Revenue can be allocated to different sponsorship pools based on governance decisions
    }
}

contract VaultBridgeBridgeAdapter {
    struct BridgeConfig {
        address bridgeContract;
        bytes4 bridgeSelector;
        bool active;
    }

    mapping(address => BridgeConfig) public bridges;
    mapping(address => address) public vbTokenToBridge;

    event BridgeAdded(address indexed bridge, address indexed vbToken);
    event CrossChainTransfer(address indexed user, address indexed vbToken, uint256 amount, uint256 destinationChain);

    function addBridge(
        address bridgeContract,
        address vbToken,
        bytes4 bridgeSelector
    ) external onlyOwner {
        bridges[vbToken] = BridgeConfig({
            bridgeContract: bridgeContract,
            bridgeSelector: bridgeSelector,
            active: true
        });

        vbTokenToBridge[vbToken] = bridgeContract;
        emit BridgeAdded(bridgeContract, vbToken);
    }

    function bridgeVbToken(
        address vbToken,
        uint256 amount,
        uint256 destinationChain,
        address recipient
    ) external {
        BridgeConfig storage config = bridges[vbToken];
        require(config.active, "Bridge not active");

        // Transfer vbTokens to this adapter
        IERC20(vbToken).transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amount);

        // Approve bridge contract
        IERC20(vbToken).approve(config.bridgeContract, amount);

        // Call bridge contract
        bytes memory callData = abi.encodeWithSelector(
            config.bridgeSelector,
            vbToken,
            amount,
            destinationChain,
            recipient
        );

        (bool success,) = config.bridgeContract.call(callData);
        require(success, "Bridge call failed");

        emit CrossChainTransfer(msg.sender, vbToken, amount, destinationChain);
    }
}

contract VaultBridgeCustomStrategy is ERC4626 {
    using SafeERC20 for IERC20;

    IERC20 public immutable underlyingAsset;

    // Multiple yield sources
    struct YieldSource {
        address protocol;
        uint256 allocation; // Percentage allocation (basis points)
        bool active;
    }

    YieldSource[] public yieldSources;
    mapping(address => uint256) public protocolBalances;

    // Risk management
    uint256 public maxSlippage = 100; // 1% in basis points
    uint256 public emergencyExitThreshold = 500; // 5% loss threshold

    event YieldSourceAdded(address indexed protocol, uint256 allocation);
    event YieldHarvested(uint256 totalYield);
    event EmergencyExit(address indexed protocol, uint256 amount);

    constructor(
        IERC20 _asset,
        string memory _name,
        string memory _symbol
    ) ERC4626(_asset) ERC20(_name, _symbol) {
        underlyingAsset = _asset;
    }

    function addYieldSource(address protocol, uint256 allocation) external onlyOwner {
        require(allocation <= 10000, "Allocation too high");

        yieldSources.push(YieldSource({
            protocol: protocol,
            allocation: allocation,
            active: true
        }));

        emit YieldSourceAdded(protocol, allocation);
    }

    function _deployAssets(uint256 assets) internal {
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < yieldSources.length; i++) {
            YieldSource storage source = yieldSources[i];
            if (!source.active) continue;

            uint256 allocatedAmount = assets * source.allocation / 10000;
            if (allocatedAmount > 0) {
                _depositToProtocol(source.protocol, allocatedAmount);
                protocolBalances[source.protocol] += allocatedAmount;
            }
        }
    }

    function _depositToProtocol(address protocol, uint256 amount) internal {
        // This would be customized based on the specific protocol
        // Examples: Compound, Aave, Morpho, etc.

        if (_isCompoundProtocol(protocol)) {
            _depositToCompound(protocol, amount);
        } else if (_isAaveProtocol(protocol)) {
            _depositToAave(protocol, amount);
        } else if (_isMorphoProtocol(protocol)) {
            _depositToMorpho(protocol, amount);
        }
    }

    function _depositToCompound(address cToken, uint256 amount) internal {
        underlyingAsset.safeApprove(cToken, amount);
        ICToken(cToken).mint(amount);
    }

    function _depositToAave(address aToken, uint256 amount) internal {
        underlyingAsset.safeApprove(aToken, amount);
        ILendingPool(aToken).deposit(address(underlyingAsset), amount, address(this), 0);
    }

    function _depositToMorpho(address morphoVault, uint256 amount) internal {
        underlyingAsset.safeApprove(morphoVault, amount);
        IMorphoVault(morphoVault).deposit(amount, address(this));
    }

    function harvestYield() external {
        uint256 totalYield = 0;

        for (uint256 i = 0; i < yieldSources.length; i++) {
            YieldSource storage source = yieldSources[i];
            if (!source.active) continue;

            uint256 currentBalance = _getProtocolBalance(source.protocol);
            uint256 deposited = protocolBalances[source.protocol];

            if (currentBalance > deposited) {
                uint256 yield = currentBalance - deposited;
                totalYield += yield;
            } else if (currentBalance < deposited * (10000 - emergencyExitThreshold) / 10000) {
                // Emergency exit if losses exceed threshold
                _emergencyExit(source.protocol);
            }
        }

        if (totalYield > 0) {
            emit YieldHarvested(totalYield);
        }
    }

    function _emergencyExit(address protocol) internal {
        uint256 balance = _getProtocolBalance(protocol);
        _withdrawFromProtocol(protocol, balance);

        // Mark protocol as inactive
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < yieldSources.length; i++) {
            if (yieldSources[i].protocol == protocol) {
                yieldSources[i].active = false;
                break;
            }
        }

        emit EmergencyExit(protocol, balance);
    }

    function _getProtocolBalance(address protocol) internal view returns (uint256) {
        // Implementation depends on specific protocol
        if (_isCompoundProtocol(protocol)) {
            return ICToken(protocol).balanceOfUnderlying(address(this));
        }
        // Add other protocols...
        return 0;
    }

    function _withdrawFromProtocol(address protocol, uint256 amount) internal {
        // Implementation depends on specific protocol
        if (_isCompoundProtocol(protocol)) {
            ICToken(protocol).redeemUnderlying(amount);
        }
        // Add other protocols...
    }

    function _isCompoundProtocol(address protocol) internal pure returns (bool) {
        // Implementation to identify Compound protocols
        return false; // Placeholder
    }

    function _isAaveProtocol(address protocol) internal pure returns (bool) {
        // Implementation to identify Aave protocols  
        return false; // Placeholder
    }

    function _isMorphoProtocol(address protocol) internal pure returns (bool) {
        // Implementation to identify Morpho protocols
        return false; // Placeholder
    }

    function totalAssets() public view override returns (uint256) {
        uint256 total = underlyingAsset.balanceOf(address(this));

        for (uint256 i = 0; i < yieldSources.length; i++) {
            if (yieldSources[i].active) {
                total += _getProtocolBalance(yieldSources[i].protocol);
            }
        }

        return total;
    }

    function _deposit(
        address caller,
        address receiver,
        uint256 assets,
        uint256 shares
    ) internal override {
        super._deposit(caller, receiver, assets, shares);
        _deployAssets(assets);
    }

    function _withdraw(
        address caller,
        address receiver,
        address owner,
        uint256 assets,
        uint256 shares
    ) internal override {
        // Withdraw from yield sources if needed
        uint256 availableAssets = underlyingAsset.balanceOf(address(this));

        if (availableAssets < assets) {
            uint256 needed = assets - availableAssets;
            _withdrawFromSources(needed);
        }

        super._withdraw(caller, receiver, owner, assets, shares);
    }

    function _withdrawFromSources(uint256 needed) internal {
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < yieldSources.length; i++) {
            if (!yieldSources[i].active) continue;

            uint256 available = _getProtocolBalance(yieldSources[i].protocol);
            uint256 toWithdraw = needed > available ? available : needed;

            if (toWithdraw > 0) {
                _withdrawFromProtocol(yieldSources[i].protocol, toWithdraw);
                protocolBalances[yieldSources[i].protocol] -= toWithdraw;
                needed -= toWithdraw;

                if (needed == 0) break;
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Vault Bridge Overview
docs.text: Vault Bridge enables chains and applications to generate native yield on Total Value Locked (TVL) by putting bridged assets to work. The protocol transforms idle bridged assets into productive capital, generating sustainable, protocol-native revenue for Layer 2 networks.

docs.title: What is Vault Bridge?
docs.text: Vault Bridge is a yield-generating mechanism that allows EVM chains to earn revenue from their TVL without requiring new infrastructure or changes to existing canonical bridges. It provides a sustainable revenue stream powered by secure yield infrastructure and expert-managed strategies.

docs.title: For Chains
docs.text:
• Native Revenue Stream: Generate sustainable revenue from bridged assets
  • No Infrastructure Changes: Works with existing bridge infrastructure
  • Customizable Parameters: Configure yield distribution and user participation
  • Scalable Revenue: Revenue grows with TVL adoption, not inflation

docs.title: For Users
docs.text:
• 1:1 Asset Representation: Receive vault bridge tokens (vbTokens) for deposited assets
  • Cross-chain Functionality: Use vbTokens in DeFi across connected chains
  • Opt-in Participation: Choose whether to participate in yield generation
  • Seamless Experience: Bridge and deposit in single transactions

docs.title: For Developers
docs.text:
• ERC-4626 Compatibility: Standard vault interface for easy integration
  • Unified Bridge Extension: Works seamlessly with Agglayer’s bridge infrastructure
  • Well-documented APIs: Comprehensive smart contract documentation
  • Proven Security: Powered by battle-tested protocols like Morpho

docs.title: Basic Flow
docs.text:
1. Asset Bridging: Users bridge assets from Layer X (primary chain) to Layer Y (secondary chain)
  2. Token Minting: Assets are deposited into Vault Bridge Token contracts, which mint vbTokens 1:1
  3. Yield Generation: Deposited assets are placed in external ERC-4626 compatible yield vaults
  4. Revenue Distribution: Generated yield is distributed to participating chains and applications
  5. Asset Utilization: vbTokens can be used in DeFi protocols on the destination chain

docs.title: Architecture Components
docs.text:
The Vault Bridge protocol consists of four main components:

  • Vault Bridge Token: ERC-20/ERC-4626 vault that handles asset deposits and vbToken minting
  • Migration Manager: Coordinates backing migration from Layer Y to Layer X
  • Native Converter: Enables direct vbToken minting on Layer Y without bridging
  • Custom Token: Allows vbTokens to be upgraded with custom behavior on Layer Y

docs.title: Supported Assets
docs.text:
Vault Bridge supports high-demand assets with available yield strategies, including:

  • WETH: Wrapped Ethereum with various staking and lending opportunities
  • USDC: USD Coin with stable yield generation strategies
  • WBTC: Wrapped Bitcoin with secure yield opportunities
  • Other ERC-20 tokens: Additional assets based on yield strategy availability

docs.title: For Agglayer-Connected Chains
docs.text:
• No fees for revenue sharing
  • Immediate compatibility with official vbTokens
  • Full Native Converter functionality support
  • Seamless bridge integration

docs.title: For Non-Agglayer Chains
docs.text:
• Third-party bridge integration required
  • Limited Native Converter functionality
  • Revenue sharing fees apply
  • Contact team for full support roadmap

docs.text:
• Non-EVM Chains: Solana (SVM), Cosmos, Move (Aptos and Sui)
  • Additional Bridges: Enhanced third-party bridge compatibility
  • Extended Functionality: Advanced yield strategies and governance features

docs.title: Yield Generation
docs.text:
• Assets deposited into Vault Bridge Token contracts generate yield through external vaults
  • Yield strategies are managed by expert risk curators (Gauntlet & Steakhouse Financial)
  • Revenue streams back to chains via native Vault Bridge contracts

docs.title: Revenue Distribution
docs.text:
• Agglayer Chains: Receive 100% of generated revenue
  • Non-Agglayer Chains: Subject to protocol fees
  • Customizable Allocation: Chains configure how revenue is distributed within their ecosystem

docs.title: Use Cases for Revenue
docs.text:
• Operations Funding: Cover chain operational costs
  • User Incentives: Sponsor transaction gas fees
  • Ecosystem Growth: Fund development and adoption initiatives
  • Governance Treasury: Build sustainable treasury reserves

docs.text:

  • Expert Curation: Risk management by Gauntlet and Steakhouse Financial
  • Proven Infrastructure: Built on battle-tested protocols like Morpho
